Error in `[.data.frame`(input, , c("ProteinName", "PeptideSequence")) : undefined columns selected

messages.subject: Re: error with PD 2.1 results
messages.subject_clean: error with PD 2.1 results
messages.body_plain:
I think I figured out what's the issue; some required columns do not exist on the default report from PD 2.1 and 2.2.

The MSstats manual has the following:

4.5.2 Preprocessing with DDA experiment from Proteome Discoverer output
PDtoMSstatsFormat function helps pre-processing for making right format of MSstats input from Proteome Discoverer output. Protein.Group.Accessions is used for ProteinName. The combination of Sequence and Modifications is used for PeptideSequence. Charge is used for PrecursorCharge. Precursor.Area is used for Intensity. In addition, there are several steps to filter out or to modify the data in order to get required information.

So according to the manual the following columns are necessary:
Protein Group Accessions
Sequence
Modifications
Charge
Precursor Area
>From that list, Protein Group Accessions and Precursor Area are not part of the default PSM, (probably because of software updates). But apparently, its just a nomenclature issue, so the question now is, which report columns should be renamed in order to the MSstats function to work ? bellow are my observations:

Protein Group Accessions
PD output contains 2 different columns with protein IDs; Master Protein Accessions and Protein Accessions. Both allow more that one ID per observation (i.e. PSM). The first one seems to be something analogous to the 'indistinguishable' protein list from other tools like ProteinProphet. The second one contains IDs from biologically distinct proteins, so it seems to me that the Master Protein Accession column should be the one to be renamed to Protein Group Accessions.

Precursor Area
There are 2 columns containing quantification information; Intensity and Area. I'm not too sure here but I think the correct one to be renamed is the Intensity column. Area seems to be related to higher levels of interpretation.

messages.subject_clean: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off
messages.body_plain:
Hi MSstats group,

Thank you for your continued support.

I have performed a targeted analysis from two mouse tissues (10-biological replicates, paired design with heavy labeled reference standards).
One tissue type was run in January, and the second several months later in April. During this period there was a substantial drop-off in instrument sensitivity (see pic).

I'd like to analyze for differentially expressed proteins (Tissue 1. v Tissue 2.)
I believe MSstats' "Equalize medians" normalization will account for this bias, but I wanted to ask to make sure.

Thanks,
Tyler

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-gkXDp8Ig9Os/WbrFPyLcT9I/AAAAAAAAAFo/0eN9CC5ySUUz7DYsFO99rJcK7_gLHFILQCLcBGAs/s1600/Systematic_Bias.png>
messages.body_snippet:
Hi MSstats group,

Thank you for your continued support.

I have performed a targeted analysis from two mouse tissues (10-biological replicates, paired design with heavy labeled reference standards).

messages.subject: Re: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off
messages.subject_clean: Systematic bias due to instrument sensitivity drop-off
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tyler,

This experiment is a non-starter from a statistical viewpoint. Since the tissue acquisitions were not randomized, you have a confounding between the tissue type and the date of data acquisition. No amount of normalization will be able to fully correct for that. This dataset in unlikely to yield any sound result. Our best advice is to start over, with an appropriate experimental design.

There are numerous examples of research that is irreproducible, due to lack of randomization. See, e.g., here  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15814023

Sincerely
OV

messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.subject_clean: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.body_plain:
1) variance from biological replicate : In your profile plot, MSstats considers the variance in green, not red. There are 6 conditions and some conditions have biological replicate. When fitting linear model, MSstats use all conditions (not use only condition you assigned), in your case, use all 6 conditions. Then, MSstats calculate linear combination for assigned comparison. So, even though one condition has one biological replicate, MSstats can analyze.
  MSstats does not have option for 'only use proteins with biological replicates between the compared conditions'. If you want, you need to filter out before using MSstats.

2) I think 'Min 2 peptides per protein' in Skyline means that Skyline will report the proteins with minimum 2 peptides. But there is no restriction for Min 2 peptides per protein per condition or min 2 peptides per all MS runs, I guess.
 MSstats has similar option that remove protein with one peptide in all converter function (like SkylinetoMSstatsFormat). But, still it does not include the restriction 'per condition'. If you want to use the proteins with at least 2 peptides for both compared conditions, you need to filter out before your analysis.

messages.subject: Missing proteins
messages.subject_clean: Missing proteins
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I was analyzing data (published) from a colleague in order to test MSstats and after running a script I realized that the main protein of interest is missing. It is being filtered out at the beginnig:

quant <- MaxQtoMSstatsFormat(evidence=infile, annotation=annot, proteinGroups=proteinGroups,
                             proteinID="proteinGroups",
                             removeProtein_with1Peptide=FALSE)

This protein was identified in all samples with over 120 MS/MS counts, MaxQuant score of 255 and is highly abundant.

After running the commands:
proteinGroups <- read.table("proteinGroups.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
infile <- read.table("evidence.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
annot <- read.csv("maxquant_annotation.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE)

proteinGroups matrix has it, ifile has it with 121 entries and then in quant it's not there.
It's not a contaminant, it's not identified by site only and not a reverse of course. Any other analysis pipelines do not filter out this protein.

I'd be happy for any help from your side.
Greetings
Witek
